title: Task 1: read a learned distribution
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 1: read a learned distribution. Define: Compare successor counts with add-one probabilities for one context character. Walk through: With vocabulary size V and context count N, add-one assigns 1/(N+V) to an unseen successor. Ask: What did smoothing assume? Expected answer and boundary: A symmetric pseudo-count over the vocabulary. It avoids zero probability but is not evidence that the successor was observed. Visual purpose: show Context > Counts > Smoothing > Normalization. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. [Sources] https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 ; https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents. Original teaching example, not an empirical deployment claim. title: Task 2: compare sampling controls
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 2: compare sampling controls. Define: Record entropy for the same logits at two positive temperatures. Walk through: Use a fixed seed per run and preserve the probability vectors, not just the sampled strings. Ask: Can two different temperatures produce the same short string? Expected answer and boundary: Yes. One sampled continuation is a noisy observation and does not identify the underlying distribution. Visual purpose: show Fixed logits | T=0.5 | T=2.0. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Task 3: reject the unknown capability
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 3: reject the unknown capability. Define: Send an unknown tool name to the same dispatcher. Walk through: Record expected status before calling the dispatcher. Verify that no accepted result is produced. Ask: Should the validator silently rename an unknown tool? Expected answer and boundary: No. Silent repair changes the requested operation. Return a specific failure and require an explicit new proposal. Visual purpose: show Unknown name > Allowlist check > Rejection > No execution. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Task 4: classify malformed readings
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 4: classify malformed readings. Define: Test empty, Boolean, string, NaN and infinite values separately. Walk through: The JSON parser rejects nonstandard constants; numeric validation also rejects nonfinite native Python values. Ask: Why keep separate tests for text and Python objects? Expected answer and boundary: They enter through different boundaries. Passing one path does not prove the other path uses the same checks. title: Task 5: stop a repeated proposal loop
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 5: stop a repeated proposal loop. Define: A cap counts every attempt, not only successful actions. Walk through: A cap of two permits at most two validations/dispatch attempts; the third event records a budget stop. Ask: What would happen if only successes counted? Expected answer and boundary: A sequence of malformed proposals could make no progress indefinitely while never reaching the cap. Visual purpose: show Attempt count > Compare cap > Validate > Append trace. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Task 6: repair syntax without changing intent
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 6: repair syntax without changing intent. Define: Correct malformed JSON manually and rerun the exact same contract. Walk through: Repair a trailing comma. Explain why the fixed string still needs semantic validation. Ask: Does syntax repair justify executing a newly added tool? Expected answer and boundary: No. A repair may change meaning. Compare fields and retain the allowlist regardless of parse success. Visual purpose: show Invalid JSON > Human review > Revised JSON > Same gates. title: Task 7: expose arithmetic with a fixture
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 7: expose arithmetic with a fixture. Define: Check mean([1,2,6]) = 3 before reading a model explanation. Walk through: A zero-mean fixture can hide a wrong denominator; [1,2,6] makes the expected result informative. Ask: What does one passing fixture establish? Expected answer and boundary: Agreement on that fixture only. Add empty, large, negative and length-bound cases before broader claims. Visual purpose: show Fixture > Independent expected value > Tool result > Compare.
